title: Reinforcement of the Aft Cargo Door Surround Longitudinal Splice Plates on ZEPHYR-24 Evo Aircraft
abstract: Thicker longitudinal splice plates and a revised fastener pattern at the aft cargo door surround of the ZEPHYR-24 Evo, introduced after door distortion was measured on aircraft operating at the increased maximum take-off weight.

sections.reason: Door closing effort measurements taken during the ZEPHYR-24 Evo weight increase campaign showed that the aft cargo door surround deflects more than the original substantiation allowed at the higher cabin differential associated with the increased maximum take-off weight. Nine aircraft reported a hard-to-close aft cargo door within their first two years of service and two reported a latch out-of-rig condition traced to surround deformation rather than to the latching mechanism itself. No cracking was found, but the deflection reduces the margin on the door seal and would eventually load the latch hooks unevenly.
sections.description: The longitudinal splice plates around the aft cargo door cut-out are replaced by items of increased gauge. The superseded intercostal D5230111892105 is removed and replaced by the current standard stringer D5230114751500, and the outboard angle JA880258-89 is added at the aft lower corner of the cut-out to close the load path into the frame. The fastener pattern along the upper and lower edges is changed from a single row to a staggered double row, and the edging grommet AES686504-33 is fitted where the wiring route passes the new fastener line. Drawings D52301146738 issue G and D52301184448 issue C carry the revised layout. Work is carried out from inside the aft cargo compartment, zones 131, 134 and 145, with the door removed and the lining panels stripped locally.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 5.2 kg per aircraft, offset to the left of the centre line by the door position, with a negligible balance effect. No electrical load change. The splice plates are one-way interchangeable: a post-modification plate may be fitted to a pre-modification aircraft but not the reverse, because the fastener pattern is denser. Door closing effort returns inside the published limit and the rigging check interval reverts to the standard value. IPC content for ATA 52-30 will be re-issued and the door rigging task in the AMM is being amended.
sections.embodiment_note: Design is frozen and production cut-in is planned for late 2023, with a retrofit bulletin to follow for delivered aircraft. Retrofit is expected to take about four days with the door removed and will normally be combined with a scheduled door overhaul.

type_data.balance_impact: Asymmetric by door position, lateral moment negligible
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN Z11468, absorbed in the section 15 build station

sections.embodiment_note: Cut in on the production line at MSN Z11468 in November 2023 and available for retrofit through a single bulletin. Retrofit takes about four days with the door removed and is normally combined with a scheduled door overhaul. It is also offered as a paired downtime package with the Cabin-Flex rear cabin conversion of MOD-154781: both apply to exactly the same aircraft type, both need the aft cargo compartment opened and the aft lining stripped, and the conversion centre now quotes one combined ground time rather than two. Done separately the operator pays a second downtime for no engineering reason.
